fields.rationale: TileLink is a chip-scale interconnect protocol, not a peripheral with an MMIO register file. There is no fixed register map in the spec. TileLink carries the integrator-defined slave address on a_address / b_address / c_address (and as d_source / d_sink / e_sink for response routing). Address-space properties (cacheability, FIFO ordering, executeability, privilege, QoS) are configured per-address-region by the SoC integrator.

address_side_field_widths.a_o_source_id_width: o bits (per-link parameter, unique per master interface)
address_side_field_widths.d_i_sink_id_width: i bits (per-link parameter, unique per slave interface)
address_side_field_widths.a_a_address_width: a bits (per-link parameter; carries the byte address)
address_side_field_widths.w_data_bus_width: w bytes (power of two, per-link parameter)

address_space_properties: FIFO ordering requirements (optional FIFO domain identifier)
fields.notes: If a future system-integration L4 is required, the canonical 'address-side fields' to capture would be: address-map regions per slave, per-region TileLink conformance level, per-region cacheability / FIFO / privilege properties, and source/sink ID allocations across the network.

evidence.quote: Properties limit what messages are allowed to be injected into a TileLink network, based on the range of addresses that the operation is targeting.
All addresses carried by TileLink channels are physical addresses. From any node in the TileLink DAG, every valid address must route over a single path to exactly one slave.
